sections.h2: Where is Horry County and what is the Grand Strand?
sections.html:
Horry County is the northeast corner of South Carolina, on the Atlantic coast against the North Carolina line. It covers 1,254.73 square miles in total, of which 1,133.31 are land and 121.42 are water, and Conway is the county seat while Myrtle Beach is the largest community.

The coastal strip around Myrtle Beach is known as the Grand Strand, and the Coast RTA bus system serves the Horry County and Grand Strand area on 15 routes. Beach communities include North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Garden City, Atlantic Beach and Briarcliffe Acres, while Loris and Aynor sit inland.

The same county tax office serves a condo near the ocean and a farmhouse near Galivants Ferry, though the buyers and the risks are very different.

sections.h2: What is the history of Horry County?
sections.html:
Horry County was created from Georgetown District in 1801, when its estimated population was 550. It is named for Revolutionary War hero Peter Horry.

Rivers and swamps isolated residents for generations, and they called the place "The Independent Republic of Horry." Even in 1950 the county had only 59,820 people.

Growth since then has been steep, and the figures show why sellers here see so many changes in a short time.

sections.h2: What does the Horry County economy depend on?
sections.html:
Tourism is the center of the local economy. Accommodation and food services employed 23.7 percent of workers in the third quarter of 2023 at an average annual wage of $29,588, and retail trade employed 18.2 percent. The county's 2022 economic output was about $18.3 billion.

  • Employers named for the county include Adidas, the City of Myrtle Beach, Coastal Carolina University, Food Lion, Hilton Grand Vacations, Publix and Walmart.
  • The county has become a destination for retirees and second-home owners.

Many Horry County properties are second homes, rentals or condos. Owners who live out of state, or who inherited a beach-area unit, often find that managing it from afar is the hard part, and that is when a quick sale makes sense.

sections.h2: How do you get around Horry County?
sections.html:
US 17, US 501, US 378, US 76 and US 701 are the main federal routes, and state routes include SC 22, SC 31, SC 90 and SC 544. Future I-73 and Future I-74 are planned corridors.

Myrtle Beach International Airport, Conway-Horry County Airport, Grand Strand Airport in North Myrtle Beach, Green Sea Airport and Twin City Airport in Loris all operate in the county. Because summer traffic on the main routes is heavy, location along those corridors shapes how buyers view a house.

sections.h2: How does flooding affect Horry County houses?
sections.html:
Flooding is a major concern in Horry County because the Waccamaw and Pee Dee rivers and the Intracoastal Waterway all run through it, and water covers about 9 percent of the county. The county's flood resilience plan says Hurricane Florence damaged more than 2,000 buildings in Horry County and closed more than 460 roads.

Florence was the third major riverine flood in four years, after Matthew and Joaquin. Bucksport, Longs, Red Bluff and Socastee are named as target communities, and Socastee has the most repetitive loss properties among them. The plan defines repetitive loss as two or more National Flood Insurance Program claims over $1,000 in ten years.

Mapping is another issue. Under the effective 1999 FEMA maps most flooded Bucksport buildings were in the minimal-risk zone, and in Socastee fewer than 20 percent of damaged buildings (96 of 565) were in the effective Special Flood Hazard Area.

If you own a flood-damaged or flood-prone house, a cash buyer who purchases as-is can take it without asking you to rebuild first.

sections.h2: When is Horry County property tax billed, and what are the due dates?
sections.html:
Horry County mails real property notices to the owner of record on October 1, and full payment is due by January 15 of the following year. Penalties take effect on January 16, February 2 and March 17, and the U.S. postmark decides whether a mailed payment is late.

The percentages are in S.C. Code 12-45-180: 3 percent, then 7 percent, then 5 percent. The county page does not list the amounts, so check your notice.

  • Treasurer phone for payments: 843-428-2126.
  • Pay at the Treasurer's Office, by mail, at a night deposit box, online or by phone. Card payments carry a convenience fee.
  • Not receiving a bill does not excuse a late payment, and the notice reflects ownership as of January 1.

sections.h2: Can you pay Horry County tax in installments?
sections.html:
Yes, for real property only, if the application is received before January 15 of the tax year. Escrowed property and personal vehicles are excluded.

The payment is the prior year's tax times 16.67 percent, made in five advance payments due February 15, April 15, June 15, August 15 and October 15. The balance is billed by November 15, and no installment is accepted after October 15.

Applications may be denied for outstanding taxes, a bank escrow account or non-ownership of the property. If you plan to sell mid-year, ask the Treasurer how the plan interacts with your closing.

sections.h2: How do reassessment and the legal residence rate work in Horry County?
sections.html:
Horry County reassesses every four years and implements in the fifth, according to its Assessor. The last was in 2019 and the next was scheduled for tax year 2024, so confirm the current cycle with the office.

Increases from a countywide reappraisal are limited to 15 percent over five years, but the cap does not apply in the year an assessable transfer of interest first becomes taxable. A sale is the usual trigger for that.

  • Legal residence, the 4 percent assessment, must be applied for between January 1 and January 15.
  • Use changes must be reported to the Assessor within six months.
  • The homestead deduction of $50,000 is for owners 65 or older, the blind, the disabled and surviving spouses, and first-time applicants apply in person at the Auditor's Office, 843-915-5051.

sections.h2: How do you appeal an Horry County assessment?
sections.html:
Request a conference in writing within 90 days of the assessment notice. In a year with no notice you can appeal at any time, and an appeal filed before the first penalty date applies to that tax year.

Your letter should include your name, the Map-Block-Parcel number, the value you think is correct and your reasons. The legal basis is S.C. Code 12-60-2510. For agricultural land that changes use, roll-back taxes apply for the year of change and four prior years.

sections.h2: What happens after Horry County taxes become delinquent?
sections.html:
Real property taxes are delinquent on March 17, and notices go out around April 1. Certified notices follow 30 days later, and levy notices are posted on delinquent properties, usually between May and October.

The sale is advertised on three consecutive Thursdays, and the redemption period is 12 months from the sale date. The Delinquent Tax Office is at 1301 Second Avenue, Conway, phone (843) 915-5472, Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm. The county said the 2026 sale date and location would appear in a November newspaper ad.

State and county recording tax on the deed is $1.85 per $500 of value under Title 12, Chapter 24. We could not open the Horry County Register of Deeds page, so ask that office about its filing steps.

faqs.q: When are Horry County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real property tax is due by January 15, and notices are mailed October 1. Penalties start on January 16, February 2 and March 17.

faqs.q: Does Horry County allow installment payments?
faqs.a: Yes, for real property if you apply before January 15. You pay 16.67 percent of last year's tax in five installments, February through October, and the balance is billed by November 15.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the 4 percent legal residence rate in Horry County?
faqs.a: File between January 1 and January 15 of the tax year. You must own and live in the home as your primary residence as of January 1.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem a house sold at an Horry County tax sale?
faqs.a: You have 12 months from the sale date. The owner, mortgage company or grantee can pay the taxes and sale costs to regain ownership.

faqs.q: Is Horry County property flood prone?
faqs.a: Parts of it are, and the county's own plan names Bucksport, Longs, Red Bluff and Socastee. Check flood zone status and insurance history before you list or sell a house.
